newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower on exports, Sparks, soybeans.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower on exports, Sparks, soybeans.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended lower after being dragged down by a host of bearish factors, traders said.

Early weakness came on reminders that U.S. wheat was priced too high to let it compete on the export scene. Traders cited news that Egypt bought 200,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat and at least 300,000 tonnes of Australian wheat.

Traders said the market lacked the consistent buying that it had seen Friday, when Cargill was a key buyer in all three U.S. wheat markets. Spillover pressure from soybeans also pressured KCBT wheat late.

Further pressure came at the midsession, when the CEO of analysts Sparks Companies said CBOT July wheat futures would trade below $3.00 per bushel during harvest next summer. CBOT July wheat closed down 2-1/2 cents at $3.30-1/2 per bushel.
Overall, KCBT wheat closed three to 5-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 5-1/4 cents at 43.96-1/4. Dec lost 5-1/2 cents to close at $4.48-1/2.

Traders said Refco bought 1.8 million March bushels but turned late seller, shedding 600,000 March bushels. FIMAT bought one million March but also sold 600,00 March. Wolcott Lincoln bear-spread one million March/Dec at 55 to 57 cents. --Greg Frost, 816 561-8671
